# Clinical Risk Distribution

This folder explores the real-world distribution of clinical risk scores and their predictive limitations in cardiovascular medicine. It specifically examines how widely used risk stratification tools, such as the CHA2DS2-VASc score, perform when applied to national registry data, revealing that a substantial proportion of severe adverse events like intracranial bleeding occur in patients classified as low thromboembolic risk. This highlights the clinical paradox of weighing anticoagulant therapy risks and benefits in cohorts traditionally considered safe from ischemic stroke.

## Pages

- [[clinical-risk-distribution|Clinical Risk Distribution]] — Analyzes the real-world distribution of CHA2DS2-VASc scores among atrial fibrillation patients who experience severe bleeding events, revealing that a large absolute number of intracranial bleeds occur in traditionally "low-risk" cohorts.
